title: ARWP Index Worthiness Practices
purpose: Decide whether a page is worth publishing into the indexable/sitemap cohort without reducing Search value to a numeric score or confusing crawl eligibility with ranking.

gates.requirement: A real user, navigation, comparison, research or decision need exists for this page. URL generation capacity is not demand.
The page contributes original, curated, calculated, normalized, first-hand or otherwise non-commodity value beyond a template and entity-name substitution.
A direct landing visitor can complete a useful task or get a complete answer without first understanding the site's internal taxonomy.
Material factual/data claims expose appropriate sources, methodology, ownership, evidence boundaries or limitations.
The page has meaningful crawlable relationships to hubs, parents, related entities, comparisons or next steps and is not merely present in a sitemap.
The page has one stable canonical URL/entity identity and does not compete with filter, query, locale, alias or generated variants.
dateModified, sitemap lastmod and release/version signals change only when the underlying page/data materially changes.
Entity/detail pages expose enough real attributes, relationships, evidence or derived insight to justify a separate page instead of a thin row wrapper.

scaledContentSignals: generated page whose uniqueValue gate is not pass
index-candidate page declared as a variantOf another URL
large generated cohort expanded before a bounded priority cohort has outcome evidence
sitemap mirrors build output instead of curated canonical index candidates
generic AI-written text is used to justify otherwise low-value records

githubPages.rule: owner.github.io/project/ is a path under one hostname, not an independent hostname-level Search site-name/favicon identity.
githubPages.action: Do not diagnose this as a missing meta-tag bug. Use page-level title/description/canonical correctly; use a custom domain or independent hostname when distinct site identity materially matters.
